1.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
Mr. Niraj Tiwari, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 is also present.

2. This criminal appeal has been filed under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, assailing the order dated 12.12.2024 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST (P.A.) Act, Bulandshahr in Bail Application No. 7218 of 2024, arising out of Case Crime No. 0089 of 2023, under Sections 147, 452, 504, 376 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act,
Police Station Khurja Nagar, District Bulandshahr.

sentences.text: This is the second bail application on behalf of the appellant.

The first prayer for bail of the appellant was considered and rejected by this Court vide order dated 6.2.2024 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 6760 of 2023.
4.

While rejecting the first bail application, this Court took note of the fact that the prosecutrix,
belonging to Scheduled Caste, was alleged to have been sexually exploited by the appellant under promise of marriage, that the appellant subsequently refused marriage on the ground of caste, and that the appellant, during earlier short-term bail, neither solemnized marriage nor surrendered on expiry thereof.

The Court had also noticed allegations that the appellant sent obscene WhatsApp messages against the victim?s counsel and the Hon?ble Judge, and further that a forged transfer certificate was filed to portray the victim as ?Rajpoot? whereas her caste certificate established her as ?Dhobi?, Scheduled Caste.
These acts were treated as serious, and on such grounds the first bail was rejected.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant now submits that although those allegations were earlier considered, the appellant has since been in custody from 20.11.2023, the charge-sheet was filed as far back as 5.4.2023 and cognizance was taken on 11.4.2023, yet not a single prosecution witness out of 12 has been examined so far.

It is urged that the trial is proceeding at a snail?s pace, the appellant has no criminal history, and continued incarceration amounts to undue hardship and pre-trial punishment.
6.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that in this case a false F.I.R. was lodged by the victim herself against the appellant for promise to marry and then established physical relations with her and then to refuse from marriage on the basis of caste of the victim.

It is further submitted that the victim was major, aged about 24 years at the time of alleged incident and agreed to marry with the appellant, then physical relations were established between both of them willingly.
No any force or coercion was used against the victim by the appellant.

It is also submitted that the victim lodged false F.I.R. against some other persons also for realizing money and in that sequence, present Deepak Giri vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85584612/
2 F.I.R. was also lodged.
7.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 as well as learned A.G.A. have opposed the prayer for bail, reiterating the earlier grounds, but could not dispute the fact that despite lapse of time since filing of charge-sheet, the trial has made no headway.
8. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.
It is true that the earlier bail was declined in view of the gravity of the allegations and conduct of the appellant, including filing of forged document and improper behaviour.

However, the law is settled that prolonged incarceration and failure of the prosecution to commence trial despite filing of charge-sheet constitute a fresh ground for bail, being a change in circumstance since the earlier rejection.

9. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature of accusations, period of custody, and the settled principle that an undertrial cannot be kept in custody indefinitely when trial is not making progress, this Court is of the view that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The impugned order dated 12.12.2024 is liable to be set aside.
10. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

11. Let the appellant Deepak Giri, involved in the aforesaid case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The appellant will cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
(iii) The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(es).
(iv) The appellant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The appellant will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

(viii) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
12.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before the competent Court.

13. As this order relates to enlargement of the appellant on bail, it is clarified that observations made in this order shall have no bearing on the merits of the case and the trial court shall not be influenced by any observation made in this order.
